evidence.fitness: Job walked: a company director or sole trader who bought kit in 2026/27 and wants the deduction for the return. Any claim with a main-pool balance (cars, brought-forward pool, second-hand kit beyond the AIA, sole-trader new kit beyond the AIA) is overstated in year 1 and the five-year run-off is wrong throughout; a sole trader above the AIA misses the 40% FYA altogether; a company period straddling 1 April 2026 gets no hybrid rate. An adviser would have to redo the computation, so the tool cannot be relied on for the year it names.
evidence.domain: Compared with CAA 2001 structure as described in the HMRC Capital Allowances Manual (CA23220 rate of WDA; AIA pro-rating; small pools; full expensing and 50% SR allowance) and the Budget 2025 measure. Sound: AIA allocation to lowest-relief expenditure first, full expensing excluded for second-hand and cars, SR FYA remainder pooled, short-period AIA/WDA scaling, cars split at 50 g/km. Departures: stale 18% main rate; no 40% FYA; no hybrid rate; long periods not scaled (unincorporated) or split (company); small-pools limit not scaled; 'Second-hand or leased' lumps leased-in kit (no allowance to a lessee) with second-hand.

defects.what: Found on the session's spot-check, not by the auditor (who scored the 53,000 as correct): the balance left after the company 50% special-rate FYA is written down at 6% in the same period. CAA 2001 s58(5) bars allocating FYA balances to a pool in the period the spend is incurred (HMRC CA23195F says the same for the 40% FYA), so 100,000 of new special-rate kit with no AIA gives 50,000 this year, not 53,000, and the test at calc.test.mjs:34 pins the wrong figure.

Main-pool WDA is 18% for a tool labelled 2026/27; it fell to 14% from 1 April 2026 (CT) and 6 April 2026 (IT). Every main-pool WDA and the five-year run-off are overstated (worked example 117,300 vs 115,300).

The 40% main-rate first-year allowance (new, unused main-rate plant from 1 January 2026, incl. unincorporated businesses and assets for leasing; excl. cars and second-hand) is not modelled; a sole trader above the AIA gets 14%/18% instead of 40%, and the finding tells sole traders they 'rely on the AIA, then 18% / 6%'.
Page, findings, README and VENTURE.yaml state 2026/27 rates and 'written down by 18% a year'; the stated year's rate is 14%.

Accounting periods of 13-18 months are accepted but AIA and WDA are capped at 12 months: an unincorporated business's allowances scale up, and a company's long period splits into two CT periods each with its own AIA (18-month 1.4m case: 1,072,000 vs 1,400,000).
No hybrid main-pool rate for a company period straddling 1 April 2026 (days-weighted 18%/14%, rounded up to 2 dp).
Tests pin the stale 18% result (3,600 / 13,600) and anchor nothing to a gov.uk figure; small-pool boundary and short-period WDA pro-rating mutants survive.
Small pools limit is a fixed GBP 1,000; it scales with the chargeable period (6 months: GBP 500), so a GBP 900 pool is wrongly written off in full.
A blank tax rate silently becomes 0% and the result reports GBP 0.00 tax saved.
Input labelled 'Second-hand or leased equipment': a lessee cannot claim allowances on leased-in kit, and new kit bought to lease out now gets the 40% FYA, not only the AIA.
AIA plan row shows internal field keys ('mainUsed', 'specialNew') to the user.

verdict: A tidy, private browser calculator whose structure follows the Capital Allowances Act: the AIA is capped, pro-rated for short periods and spent on second-hand and special-rate items first, full expensing and the 50% special-rate allowance are company-only, and the small pool is written off. It does not meet the bar because it is wrong for the year it names. The main-pool WDA is 18% in a tool labelled 2026/27, when gov.uk's Budget 2025 measure cut it to 14% from April 2026, so the worked example deducts 117,300 where 115,300 is right and every run-off year is overstated; the new 40% main-rate FYA from 1 January 2026 is missing, so a sole trader buying beyond the AIA loses at least 44,000 of first-year relief on 1.2m; long periods are capped at 12 months and straddling periods get no hybrid rate. The tests pin the stale 18% figure. Setting mainWda to 0.14 and correcting the 18% text and test is a one-line safe fix; the 40% FYA, hybrid rate and long-period handling need a small feature PR. Its own kill criterion (a rate differing from GOV.UK) is met.
